title: Windows LBFO NIC Team Degradation
exclusions: Monitors host-level Windows Server Load Balancing/Failover (LBFO) teams returned by `Get-NetLbfoTeam` and `Get-NetLbfoTeamMember`; it does not monitor Switch Embedded Teaming, Hyper-V virtual-switch teams, Network ATC intents, storage-only adapters, guest virtual NICs, switch-side LACP state, cable optics, upstream ports, routing, DNS, firewall policy, end-to-end packet loss, or application reachability. A returned row means a complete local snapshot reports team status other than `Up` or at least one member with `OperationalStatus=Failed` or `FailureReason` other than `NoFailure`; it does not identify the physical root cause. Optional Network Interface error/discard counters are corroborating telemetry, not the team-state authority. The five-minute collection cadence, two-minute allowance, immediate one-snapshot notification, recovery rule, and retention are local policy choices rather than Microsoft or Splunk defaults. This UC does not enable/disable adapters, change Active/Standby mode, alter teaming mode/load balancing, restart networking, or attest compliance.
evidence: After deployment, retain the version-controlled `TA_windows_lbfo_health` collector and hash; qualified Windows/NetLbfo/Splunk versions; approved inventory of hosts, teams, configured members, owners, and maintenance windows; read-only execution identity; effective PowerShell input and JSON parsing; every accepted manifest and team row; rejected-snapshot source-health output; `windows_lbfo_nic_team_degradation` saved-search definition/ACL/schedule/dispatch; same-time `Get-NetLbfoTeam`, `Get-NetLbfoTeamMember`, `Get-NetAdapter`, and switch-side comparisons; relevant Network Interface counter samples; alert dispositions; bounded exceptions; and dated positive, negative, malformed, incomplete, duplicate, stale, boundary, recovery, and scale tests. This documentation-only review created no collector, event, saved search, alert, dashboard, network change, or production evidence.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In an isolated index with fixed event and dispatch times, emit one schema-1 complete manifest and one LBFO team row for `host=hv-lab-01`, `team_name=Prod-Team`, the latest aligned five-minute `sample_epoch`, one `snapshot_id`, `configured_member_count=2`, `observed_member_count=2`, `team_status=Degraded`, `failed_member_count=1`, `failed_members=Ethernet 2`, and `failure_reasons=PhysicalMediaDisconnected`. Expect exactly one result preserving all identity, count, status, failure, snapshot, event/index time, and `use_case=UC-1.2.117` fields. Repeat with `team_status=Up` and one failed member; expect one member-failure result.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Run isolated variants and expect zero primary rows for each: one complete team with `team_status=Up`, equal configured/observed member counts, and zero failed members; wrong index/source/source type/schema/record type; no manifest; two manifests; `snapshot_complete=0`; expected team count unequal to emitted team rows; duplicate team name; configured member count unequal to observed count; failed count greater than observed count; blank status; future, fractional, stale, or non-five-minute sample epoch; tied snapshot IDs for one host/sample; and a healthy older snapshot when the latest expected sample is missing. Source health must report every rejected or absent snapshot. A bounded maintenance exception may suppress delivery only after the base result and must not change base result count.

dataSources: Primary source: a deployment-owned PowerShell collector on each governed Windows Server LBFO host runs Microsoft `Get-NetLbfoTeam` and `Get-NetLbfoTeamMember` every five minutes and emits complete JSON snapshots to deployment-chosen `index=windows`, local `source=windows_lbfo_team_health`, local `sourcetype=ms:windows:lbfo:team`. Required fields are `schema_version, record_type, host, sample_epoch, snapshot_id, snapshot_epoch, snapshot_complete, expected_team_count, team_name, team_status, teaming_mode, load_balancing_algorithm, configured_member_count, observed_member_count, failed_member_count, failed_members, failure_reasons`. Optional Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows `Perfmon:Network_Interface` events collect `Packets Received Errors`, `Packets Outbound Errors`, `Packets Received Discarded`, and `Packets Outbound Discarded` for diagnosis.
app: A version-controlled deployment app such as `TA_windows_lbfo_health` supplies the read-only PowerShell collector, complete-snapshot JSON contract, source-health search, primary saved search, dashboard, fixtures, and bounded exception lookup. Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (`Splunk_TA_windows`, Splunkbase 742) 10.0.1 or a later compatible release is optional for supported Network Interface performance-counter collection; it does not provide the custom LBFO team-state snapshot.

description: Detects each governed Windows Server LBFO team whose latest complete five-minute PowerShell snapshot reports team status other than `Up` or one or more members with failed operational/failure-reason state. One result represents one team and preserves the team mode, configured-versus-observed member counts, failing member names/reasons, snapshot identity, and collection/index times.
value: An LBFO team can continue carrying traffic after one member fails, hiding loss of redundancy until another link, adapter, driver, or switch path fails. Complete team/member snapshots expose that degraded safety margin before a second fault becomes an outage, while explicit inventory and source-health checks prevent a missing collector or disappeared member from being reported as a healthy team.
implementation: Deploy a signed `TA_windows_lbfo_health` PowerShell collector only to Windows Server hosts with governed LBFO teams. Every five minutes, join `Get-NetLbfoTeam` to `Get-NetLbfoTeamMember`, validate configured/observed membership, derive failed members from `OperationalStatus=Failed` or `FailureReason!=NoFailure`, and emit one complete manifest plus one JSON row per team. Save the supplied SPL as `windows_lbfo_nic_team_degradation`, schedule it two minutes after each sample, and notify on the first accepted snapshot whose team is not `Up` or has a failed member. Operate missing/incomplete/duplicate snapshot health and recovery separately; use Network Interface error/discard counters only as diagnostic context.
visualization: Dashboard `Windows — LBFO Team Health`: show expected-host snapshot health first; then status tiles for healthy, degraded, failed-member, missing, and maintenance teams. Provide a table with `host, team_name, team_status, teaming_mode, load_balancing_algorithm, configured_member_count, observed_member_count, failed_member_count, failed_members, failure_reasons, event_time, owner, exception`. Add 24-hour status timelines, a host/team/member matrix, seven-day failure counts, and optional per-member error/discard counter deltas. Drill down to the accepted raw JSON/manifest, same-time PowerShell output, adapter state/statistics, approved change, and switch-port evidence. Never render missing or rejected snapshots as `Up`.
schema: Custom complete Windows Server LBFO team/member JSON snapshot
dataModelAcceleration: Not applicable to the primary alert. The Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows does not map `Perfmon:Network_Interface` to a CIM data model, and generic Change/Endpoint summaries do not preserve LBFO team/member identity, status, failure reason, configured-versus-observed membership, or complete-snapshot controls. A purpose-built summary may be used only after raw parity and source-health tests; `tstats count` cannot establish team redundancy.

knownFalsePositives:
A result is a real degraded/non-Up LBFO team or failed-member state in an accepted local snapshot. It can still be expected or less urgent under a controlled change; do not call the measurement false merely because the service remains reachable.

1. **Approved adapter, driver, firmware, or Windows servicing** — A rollout can temporarily reset a member or rebuild its link. Compare exact host/member, package and driver version, deployment job, maintenance ticket, start/end, peer-team state, and switch port. Use an exact host/team/member delivery exception limited to the approved window; never ignore all teams during Patch Tuesday.

2. **Network-switch port, optic, cable, or LACP maintenance** — A network engineer may intentionally remove one path while preserving service on another. Correlate switch change, port-channel/LACP member state, optic diagnostics, cabling record, team mode, remaining active capacity, and maintenance end. Suppress only the named team/member until the exclusive expiry and require post-change `Up` evidence.

3. **Planned LBFO failover test** — Operations may disconnect or disable one member to prove redundancy. Match the exercise ID, operator, host/team/member list, expected failure reason, start/end, traffic validation, and rollback. Retain the detector result as test evidence; suppress paging only for the exercise window.

4. **Intentional Active/Standby operation** — Microsoft documents Active and Standby administrative modes, and a standby member can become active when another member fails. Administrative mode alone is not a fault and is not used by the SPL. Investigate only when team status is not `Up` or the member reports a failure; compare the approved team design before changing roles.

5. **Host build, cluster-node drain, or decommission** — A host being staged, isolated, or retired can have links removed while monitoring is still enabled. Verify CMDB lifecycle, cluster drain/evacuation, service placement, shutdown plan, and retirement epoch. Disable the governed inventory/collector through versioned policy after retirement rather than adding an open-ended exception.

6. **Lab or disaster-recovery host with deliberately disconnected backup paths** — A nonproduction or cold-standby server may retain an LBFO definition while switch ports are intentionally unavailable. Confirm environment/activation plan, owner, expected member state, test cadence, and service isolation. Model it with a distinct policy and bounded dormant period; do not let its exception match production.

**Safe notification suppression:** apply lookup windows_lbfo_team_exceptions.csv only after the base result, keyed by exact lowercase `host,team_name` and, when present, exact failed member. Require inclusive `valid_from_epoch`, exclusive `valid_until_epoch`, owner, approver, ticket, reason, expected status, and rollback/test evidence. Reject wildcards, host-only rules, open-ended dates, and any exception for missing, incomplete, duplicate, stale, malformed, count-inconsistent, or inventory-mismatched snapshots. Preserve the finding and exception. Close only after two consecutive complete five-minute snapshots report team `Up`, zero failed members, and configured/observed member counts equal; missing data cannot recover.
mitreAttack: N/A (operational Windows Server LBFO redundancy monitoring; no adversary behavior or intent is asserted)
hardware: Windows Server 2012 or later systems using native LBFO NIC Teaming and exposing the NetLbfo PowerShell module. Hyper-V Switch Embedded Teaming, Network ATC/Azure Local intents, vendor-specific teaming drivers, Windows client systems, guest virtual adapters, and upstream switch/optic/cable telemetry require separate collection contracts.

scriptExample:
```powershell
# Illustrative collector core; production code must add policy/inventory validation,
# non-overlap, signed deployment, error records, atomic output, and tests.
$SampleEpoch = [int64]([Math]::Floor([DateTimeOffset]::UtcNow.ToUnixTimeSeconds() / 300) * 300)
$SnapshotEpoch = [DateTimeOffset]::UtcNow.ToUnixTimeSeconds()
$SnapshotId = [guid]::NewGuid().ToString()
$HostId = $env:COMPUTERNAME.ToLowerInvariant()
$Teams = @(Get-NetLbfoTeam -ErrorAction Stop)
$Members = @(Get-NetLbfoTeamMember -ErrorAction Stop)
$Rows = foreach ($Team in $Teams) {
  $TeamMembers = @($Members | Where-Object { [string]$_.Team -eq [string]$Team.Name })
  $Failed = @($TeamMembers | Where-Object {
    [string]$_.OperationalStatus -eq 'Failed' -or [string]$_.FailureReason -ne 'NoFailure'
  })
  [ordered]@{
    schema_version=1; record_type='team'; host=$HostId; sample_epoch=$SampleEpoch
    snapshot_id=$SnapshotId; snapshot_epoch=$SnapshotEpoch; team_name=[string]$Team.Name
    team_status=[string]$Team.Status; teaming_mode=[string]$Team.TeamingMode
    load_balancing_algorithm=[string]$Team.LoadBalancingAlgorithm
    configured_member_count=@($Team.Members).Count; observed_member_count=$TeamMembers.Count
    failed_member_count=$Failed.Count; failed_members=($Failed.Name -join ';')
    failure_reasons=(($Failed | ForEach-Object { "$($_.Name)=$($_.FailureReason)" }) -join ';')
  }
}
$Rows | ForEach-Object { $_ | ConvertTo-Json -Compress }
[ordered]@{schema_version=1;record_type='manifest';host=$HostId;sample_epoch=$SampleEpoch;snapshot_id=$SnapshotId;snapshot_epoch=$SnapshotEpoch;snapshot_complete=1;expected_team_count=$Rows.Count} | ConvertTo-Json -Compress
```
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites and exact monitoring contract

Assign Windows platform, server-hardware, network/switch, virtualization/cluster, Splunk collection/content, source-health, service-desk, and incident owners. Inventory only hosts that actually use native Windows Server LBFO: stable host ID, team name, configured member names/interface descriptions/GUIDs, team mode, load-balancing algorithm, Active/Standby design, switch/port-channel mapping, service and cluster role, owner, maintenance calendar, and retirement time. Microsoft documents that NetLbfo NIC Teaming is a Windows Server feature and that `Get-NetLbfoTeam` returns teams while `Get-NetLbfoTeamMember` returns the adapters belonging to them.

Do not deploy this contract to Switch Embedded Teaming or Network ATC. For SET, use `Get-VMSwitchTeam`; for Network ATC, Microsoft directs administrators to `Get-NetIntentStatus` and owns the host network configuration. Mixing these technologies produces missing cmdlets or false health conclusions. Qualify the exact Windows Server, NetLbfo object properties, PowerShell handler, Universal Forwarder, custom app, optional Microsoft Windows add-on, parsing tier, and Splunk platform versions in nonproduction. The collector needs read-only local access to the NetLbfo objects and stdout to its own Splunk input; it needs no right to add/remove members, change Active/Standby mode, alter teaming/load-balancing, disable adapters, or modify switch configuration.

The primary threshold is categorical and immediate: in the latest accepted five-minute snapshot, `team_status` not equal to `Up` OR `failed_member_count>0` returns one row per team. There is no evidence-based packet-count threshold for LBFO failure. A cadence of 5 minutes and one sample are example operational choices: use a shorter qualified cadence for ultra-critical paths or require persistence only if the resulting delay is acceptable. Recovery requires two complete consecutive samples with status `Up`, zero failed members, and equal configured/observed counts. Missing data never means recovery.

## Step 1 — Collect one complete LBFO snapshot

Run `Get-NetLbfoTeam -ErrorAction Stop` and `Get-NetLbfoTeamMember -ErrorAction Stop` locally. Before production coding, inspect both with `Format-List *` and `Get-Member` on every supported Windows build. Preserve observed strings rather than inventing numeric mappings. Join each member by the documented `Team` association to the team `Name`. Compare `@($Team.Members).Count` with joined member count; a mismatch makes the snapshot invalid rather than healthy.

For each team preserve `Name`, `Status`, `TeamingMode`, `LoadBalancingAlgorithm`, configured/observed member counts, and diagnostics for members whose displayed `OperationalStatus` is `Failed` or `FailureReason` is not `NoFailure`. Microsoft documents Active/Standby as administrative roles: Standby does not participate until another member fails, so administrative mode by itself is not a fault and must not page. Preserve complete member objects in restricted diagnostic output if needed, but keep the compact primary row free of MAC/IP data.

Create one five-minute UTC `sample_epoch` aligned to a multiple of 300, actual integer `snapshot_epoch`, and UUID `snapshot_id`. Emit one `team` JSON row per configured team and one `manifest` only after both cmdlets, joins, and validations succeed. `expected_team_count` must equal emitted rows and distinct team names. Set `snapshot_complete=1` only on full success. A governed host with zero teams, a cmdlet exception, missing member, duplicate team, blank property, partial stdout, or policy/inventory mismatch must emit a separate collector-health event and no complete manifest. Prevent overlapping executions and write JSON lines atomically.

The `scriptExample` is an illustrative core, not production-ready code. Production must validate the approved team inventory, prove exact object properties, catch/serialize errors separately, reject duplicate names, protect against formatting-stream output, preserve code revision, and emit manifest last. Package it in `TA_windows_lbfo_health`; do not modify `Splunk_TA_windows/default`.

## Step 2 — Configure Splunk transport and optional counters

Configure an app-owned local PowerShell input on each Windows host:

```ini
[powershell://windows_lbfo_team_health]
script = . "$SplunkHome\etc\apps\TA_windows_lbfo_health\bin\collect-lbfo-health.ps1"
schedule = */5 * * * *
source = windows_lbfo_team_health
sourcetype = ms:windows:lbfo:team
index = windows
disabled = 0
```

Splunk documents that the PowerShell input indexes command/script output and accepts seconds or cron schedule. On Splunk Cloud it runs on a customer-managed Windows forwarder, not the managed search tier. Verify the syntax and service identity on the qualified release. Configure one JSON object per event with `KV_MODE=json`, no line merging, and a measured `TRUNCATE`; confirm effective configuration with `splunk btool inputs list powershell://windows_lbfo_team_health --debug` and `splunk btool props list ms:windows:lbfo:team --debug`.

For diagnostics, optionally enable Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows `perfmon://Network_Interface` in a deployment-local file. Microsoft identifies `Packets Received Errors`, `Packets Outbound Errors`, `Packets Received Discarded`, and `Packets Outbound Discarded` as potential-network-problem counters. Splunk requires exact object/counter names and documents `Perfmon:Network_Interface`/`PerfmonMk:Network_Interface`. Validate available localized names with Windows Performance Monitor or `typeperf`; use the add-on's supported English-name setting where qualified. These cumulative/error values need per-interface deltas, resets, and traffic context. Do not assert that one positive error, a universal percentage, or `Output Queue Length>2` proves an LBFO member failed; use them to explain a state finding.

## Step 3 — Establish source health before team state

Maintain a governed inventory of expected hosts/teams/members and compare every sample. Report a missing latest host or team after one cadence plus measured indexing allowance; no/multiple manifest; incomplete manifest; expected/event/distinct team mismatch; configured/observed member mismatch; unknown/duplicate team; tied snapshot IDs; stale/future/fractional/misaligned epoch; `_time` mismatch; wrong source/type/schema; blank status/mode/algorithm; invalid counts; collector exception; code/version drift; and unexplained team/member inventory changes.

Route source health to Windows and Splunk owners. A host can disappear because its network path failed—the exact condition being monitored—so no data is high-priority unknown state, not green. A missing member is rejected before the primary rule and must be visible as source/configuration health. Preserve `_indextime` and measure p99 collection/forwarding delay.

The SPL expects `floor((now()-120)/300)*300`, allowing 2 minutes after each boundary. Schedule the search after that allowance. If normal latency approaches 2 minutes, fix collector runtime, queues, receivers, indexing, or clocks before widening the delay and updating SPL/tests. Keep the 20-minute raw horizon only to tolerate dispatch; the latest-slot predicate prevents an old degraded sample from replacing missing current state.

## Step 4 — Create and understand the saved search

Save the sidecar SPL verbatim as `windows_lbfo_nic_team_degradation` and trigger when result count is greater than zero. Numeric conversion prevents lexical count/epoch comparisons. The base predicates require local schema 1, manifest/team record types, stable host/snapshot identity, aligned integer sample time, actual collection within two minutes, and event time within two minutes of collection.

`valid_team` requires identity/status/mode/algorithm and integral, self-consistent member counts. `eventstats` requires exactly one manifest and equality among expected, actual, valid, and distinct teams. A second accepted snapshot ID for one host/slot is rejected. Only then does the search keep team rows, select the newest expected slot, normalize status, and label `team_status`, `member_failure`, or both. Unknown nonblank status is conservatively non-Up and pages; field changes should first be caught in validation/source health.

The rule intentionally does not search driver provider names or localized event-message regex. Intel, NVIDIA/Mellanox, VMware, and other driver providers use product/version-specific events that are not a stable universal LBFO contract. It also corrects the old generated event-ID mapping, which assigned unverified meanings to FailoverClustering/NLB/NDIS events. Team/member cmdlets are the direct local authority for this title.

Operate recovery outside the trigger using two accepted consecutive healthy samples. Group/throttle by exact host/team, retain every evaluation, and reopen if either branch persists. Apply exceptions after base output only.

## Step 5 — Validate Windows, JSON, SPL, counters, and scale

Use isolated indexes and fixed dispatch time for the exact `controlTest`. Assert one manifest, one row per team, count equality, five-minute alignment, accepted latest slot, status case normalization, each breach reason, and exact output columns. Test zero teams, duplicate names, member-count mismatch, malformed JSON/numbers, null properties, partial output, two snapshots in one slot, old-only degradation, `_time`/snapshot skew, delayed indexing, Unicode/spaces in names, semicolons in diagnostic strings, and recovery. Source health must identify all invalid variants while the primary search returns none.

On a nonproduction LBFO host, capture same-time:

```powershell
Get-NetLbfoTeam | Format-List *
Get-NetLbfoTeamMember | Format-List *
Get-NetAdapter | Format-List Name,InterfaceDescription,Status,LinkSpeed,InterfaceGuid
Get-NetAdapterStatistics | Format-List *
```

Compare raw objects to emitted JSON and Splunk fields. Perform a planned failover test only with network/cluster/service approval: validate traffic redundancy first, remove one test member path, observe team/member state and one result, restore it, then prove two healthy recovery samples. Never disable a production link solely for monitoring. For LACP, compare switch port-channel/member state; for SwitchIndependent, compare independent upstream paths.

Validate optional counters in Performance Monitor and raw `Perfmon:Network_Interface`; prove interface-instance mapping survives adapter rename and that counter reset on reboot/driver reload does not become a negative delta. Measure collector duration/CPU/output, PowerShell-handler contention, indexed bytes, search runtime, and dashboard cardinality at fleet scale. Keep `status=draft` until owners accept versions, permissions, inventory, collector, source health, fixtures, failover test, alert delivery, dashboard, suppression expiry, recovery, and runbook.

## Step 6 — Operationalize response, suppression, and review

Build the dashboard described in `visualization`, use UTC or label timezone, and put unknown/missing state above healthy teams. Severity depends on team state, failed/remaining members, team mode, traffic, host/service criticality, cluster failover, switch path, and second-fault exposure. A degraded four-member backup network is not equivalent to a two-member production/storage path with one member left.

Alert text should say `Windows LBFO team redundancy degraded: <host>/<team>`. Include team status/mode/algorithm, configured/observed/failed counts, failing names/reasons, sample/snapshot/index time, source health, owner, service/cluster role, exception, optional counter deltas, and runbook.

Responder sequence:
1. Verify accepted manifest, latest sample, exact host/team, counts, raw JSON, collector/source health, and no expired exception.
2. Run the same team/member/adapter/statistics cmdlets locally or through approved management and preserve output/time.
3. Confirm application and cluster health, traffic path, remaining redundancy, Active/Standby design, recent Windows/driver/firmware/team changes, and host lifecycle.
4. Correlate switch port-channel/LACP member, interface/link/optic/cable state, VLAN, errors/discards, and maintenance ticket with network owners.
5. Choose reviewed remediation: restore cable/optic/switch port, correct LACP/port-channel, roll back or repair driver/firmware, reattach the approved adapter, or fail service/cluster workload away. Do not mutate teaming from the alert action.
6. Validate service traffic, team `Up`, zero failed members, equal counts, switch state, and two complete recovery samples before closure.
7. Preserve cause, remediation, counter/switch evidence, and any inventory/policy change.

Review inventory, versions, team design, switch mapping, thresholds/cadence, owners, exceptions, and dashboard quarterly and after hardware, driver, firmware, Windows, team, switch, cluster, Splunk, or organizational changes.

## Step 7 — Troubleshoot without hiding loss of redundancy

- **No snapshots:** verify the host is expected/reachable, NetLbfo module/team exists, PowerShell input assignment/service identity, script signature, forwarder queues, index routing, JSON parsing, and source-health alert. No data is not `Up`.
- **`Get-NetLbfoTeam` returns no objects:** confirm this is an LBFO host rather than SET/ATC, team feature/configuration, host inventory, and decommission state. Do not emit a complete zero-team manifest for a governed LBFO host.
- **Configured/observed count mismatch:** inspect `Team.Members`, `Get-NetLbfoTeamMember`, adapter rename/removal, driver update, concurrent reconfiguration, and collector join. Preserve and reject; do not lower expected count automatically.
- **Team `Degraded` but no failed members:** inspect full team/member objects, team interface, LACP negotiation, switch state, VMQ/RSS/driver/firmware, and timing. Team status alone correctly triggers.
- **Member failed but team `Up`:** preserve the member-failure branch; verify object values and remaining path. Do not wait for complete team failure.
- **Standby member appears:** compare `AdministrativeMode` and documented design. The collector does not fail a member solely for Standby; investigate only explicit failed status/reason or team non-Up.
- **All fields null or strings changed:** inspect raw cmdlet objects with `Get-Member`, script serialization, PowerShell/add-on/Windows version, and JSON extraction. Fail source health rather than editing SPL to accept unqualified values.
- **Counter spike without team fault:** compare packets/traffic, counter reset, adapter statistics, switch errors/discards, and packet capture. Counter evidence is diagnostic, not the primary threshold.
- **Duplicate snapshots:** check overlapping PowerShell executions, duplicate app deployment, local plus remote collection, and forwarding replay. Correct collection; do not arbitrary-dedup one authority.
- **Alert remains after repair:** verify the newest expected sample, collector/indexing delay, status strings, count parity, and two-sample recovery. Missing or one healthy sample cannot close.
grandmaExplanation: We check the group of network sockets a Windows server uses for backup connectivity. If one path fails while the others keep traffic moving, we warn the team before another failure takes the server offline.
